content: Severe hypotension or syncope may occur, and close monitoring is recommended. Fluconazole can increase the levels or effects of darunavir by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir can increase the levels or effects of fludrocortisone through the same mechanism, while fludrocortisone may decrease the levels or effects of darunavir. Close monitoring is necessary. Darunavir also increases the levels or effects of inhaled flunisolide via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fluoxetine through other mechanisms, necessitating caution and monitoring. Darunavir similarly increases fluoxetine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. When co-administering SSRIs, TCAs, or trazodone, dose titration of the antidepressant to the lowest feasible dose is recommended, with close monitoring of antidepressant response. Darunavir increases flurazepam levels through CYP3A4 metabolism, and alternative therapies should be considered if available. Cobicistat also increases flurazepam levels, requiring caution and monitoring. Cobicistat and darunavir both increase the levels or effects of flutamide via CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used, as co-administration is not recommended. Cobicistat increases the levels of fluticasone furoate, and darunavir has a similar effect. For intranasal fluticasone, co-administration with darunavir should be avoided due to the risk of systemic corticosteroid adverse effects, including Cushing-type symptoms. Cobicistat increases the levels of fluvastatin via CYP3A4 metabolism, and darunavir has a similar effect. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with darunavir, start with the lowest recommended dose and titrate while monitoring for safety. Fluvoxamine increases cobicistat levels through other mechanisms, requiring caution and monitoring. Fluvoxamine also increases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating close monitoring. Darunavir increases fosamprenavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases fosaprepitant levels, and fosaprepitant increases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Cobicistat also increases fosaprepitant levels, requiring alternative drugs. Fosphenytoin decreases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and co-administration is contraindicated. Fosphenytoin also decreases cobicistat levels, making co-administration contraindicated. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Cobicistat increases futibatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and co-administration should be avoided due to the risk of futibatinib toxicities. Darunavir increases gefitinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of gefitinib adverse effects. Darunavir increases gepirone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and co-administration is contraindicated. Cobicistat also increases gepirone levels, making co-administration contraindicated. Cobicistat increases gilteritinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and alternative drugs should be used. Darunavir has a similar effect, and co-administration should be avoided. Cobicistat increases the levels of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir via CYP3A4 metabolism, and darunavir decreases its metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended. Darunavir decreases the effects of glimepiride, glipizide, and glyburide, with reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Caution and monitoring are advised. Grapefruit increases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Green tea may increase the risk of bleeding when combined with darunavir. Griseofulvin decreases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Darunavir increases guanfacine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. The guanfacine dosage should be reduced to half the recommended dose when co-administered. Cobicistat also increases guanfacine levels, and alternative drugs should be considered. Cobicistat increases haloperidol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and darunavir has a similar effect. Close monitoring is required. Darunavir increases hydrocodone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may result in potentially fatal respiratory depression. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Darunavir increases hydrocortisone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while hydrocortisone decreases darunavir levels. Close monitoring is required. Darunavir increases hydroxyprogesterone caproate levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Cobicistat increases ibrutinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and darunavir has a similar effect. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. If short-term use of a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is necessary, interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. Idelalisib increases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and co-administration should be avoided. Cobicistat increases idelalisib levels, and idelalisib increases cobicistat levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Cobicistat decreases ifosfamide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and darunavir has a similar effect. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Darunavir increases iloperidone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and iloperidone increases darunavir levels. Close monitoring is required. Cobicistat increases imatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and darunavir has a minor effect. Close monitoring is recommended. Darunavir increases imipramine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and co-administration with SSRIs, TCAs, or trazodone may require dose titration of the antidepressant to the lowest feasible dose. Cobicistat increases indinavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and co-administration is contraindicated. Darunavir increases indinavir levels, and both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Co-administration is not recommended. Cobicistat increases infigratinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and darunavir has a similar effect. Co-administration should be avoided. Darunavir decreases the effects of insulin aspart, insulin degludec, and other insulins due to insulin resistance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Cobicistat increases irinotecan levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and darunavir has a similar effect. Co-administration is contraindicated. Cobicistat increases isavuconazonium sulfate levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and co-administration is contraindicated. Cobicistat increases isradipine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and darunavir has a minor effect. Close monitoring is recommended. Darunavir increases istradefylline levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and therapy modification is required. Cobicistat increases itraconazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and darunavir has a similar effect. Co-administration is not recommended. Itraconazole increases cobicistat levels, and alternative drugs should be considered. Cobicistat increases ivabradine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and darunavir has a similar effect. Co-administration is contraindicated. Cobicistat increases ivacaftor levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and darunavir has a similar effect. Ivacaftor dosage should be reduced when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Cobicistat increases ivosidenib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and darunavir has a similar effect. Co-administration should be avoided. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. Darunavir increases ixabepilone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and cobicistat has a similar effect. Co-administration should be avoided. Darunavir decreases ketamine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Cobicistat increases ketoconazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and darunavir has a similar effect. Co-administration is not recommended.
